items.label: f02-tests-overstate
items.front: Two ways the support-hub unit tests overstate their coverage
items.back: The SLA test asserts only the PAUSED label, not resume or accumulation. The schema test passes five invalid fields at once and asserts success === false, so any one rule would make it pass and it cannot say which rule rejected the payload.

items.label: f04-wall-clock-sla
items.front: How are SLA deadlines computed, and what is missing?
items.back: createdAt + N wall-clock minutes. No business hours, holidays or time zones: a 24-hour target set Friday 17:00 UTC falls due Saturday 17:00 UTC; paused time is never credited.

items.label: f03-sla-job-limits
items.back: Nothing calls it. It also runs each ticket's writes outside a transaction, loads every active ticket with no paging, sets isEscalated even when it skips the escalation record, and never sets status ESCALATED. Dashboard 'breached' counts therefore show whatever was persisted at the last write.

items.label: f01-transition-table
items.front: The ticket state machine: shape and the paths that bypass it
items.back: An adjacency map with 25 allowed edges between 7 states, plus a free pass for self-transitions. Only changeTicketStatus consults it; addPublicReply and escalateTicket write status directly.
